diagnosis.summary: Checkout‑API latency spiked after the 10:15 Z deployment of v4.17, reaching a p95 of 2,150 ms from a baseline of 200 ms. The spike was caused by a reduced database connection pool size that saturated orders‑DB connections.
diagnosis.root_cause: The new config in commit a91f3c2 set the orders‑DB pool to max_connections:10 and acquire_timeout_ms:2000, causing ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and long db.pool.acquire spans.

evidence.finding: p95 jumped from 200 ms to 2,150 ms within minutes of the release
orders-db pool max_connections=10, in_use=10, waiting=143, acquire_wait_p95_ms≈1,800 ms
212 ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and 504 upstream timeout logs in last 15 min

ruled_out: Payment gateway slowdown – payment-gateway.authorize span ≈187 ms with no errors
Inventory API issue – no latency spikes or errors in inventory‑api logs
Network partition – only DB acquire timeouts observed

proposal.rationale: The latency spike is caused by a reduced orders‑DB connection pool in the new v4.17 release, leading to ConnectionPoolTimeoutError and long db.pool.acquire spans. Rolling back to the previous stable version v4.16 restores the original pool size (max_connections >10) and eliminates the queueing, as demonstrated in similar incidents (INC-4630). This is the safest remediation that directly addresses the root cause without affecting other services.
